name: Mother Sallowmire
role: The marsh-hag of the stilts: she helps the desperate, and she is always, always paid
knowledge: What every family on the stilts owes her, and in what coin
Which herbs in the marsh heal and which only look like it
The true names of three people who sold them to her and were never missed
wants: To be paid in something she hasn't already got; she has been paid in years for so long she has more of them than she wants
fears: That someone will pay her in kindness, and she will not know what to do with it.
The day the stilts have no one desperate left.
appearance: A bent old woman in a coat of patched reed-cloth, with a face like a walnut and startlingly young green eyes. There is always something bubbling behind her, and she is always, somehow, already expecting you.
voiceHints: Sweet as honey, then suddenly sharp. Calls everyone 'duck'. Names the price before you ask and never haggles.

abilities.why: she can give, and she can take
veilwright secondary: she tells you a kinder version of what she took
the young eyes are not hers
threnodist tertiary: she sings for the ones who paid too much

physicality: Small, bent, quick-handed. What catches the eye: the green eyes, which are younger than she is by a lifetime or two.
questSeeds: A child on the stilts is dying and the family has already paid her once this year. She will save the child for a price the player has to carry instead.
Someone has been paying her in stolen years: other people's. She wants the thief found, not because it is wrong, but because it is her trade.
storyRule: The Rootkin tale holds: she cannot refuse a fair bargain once it's spoken aloud, and she cannot take what is freely given. A gift, freely given, is the one coin that binds her.
gear: a bone ladle and a pot that is never empty
a string of little knotted cords, each one a year
a green glass eye she keeps in her pocket
_authoredWhy: SNG-661 §5. The hag as a Rootkin story: the bargain for life, paid in life. Among refugees, because that is where desperate people are.
